name: South Korea

flag.description: A white field with a red-and-blue taegeuk (yin-yang) circle in the centre, red on top, and a black trigram of three broken or unbroken bars near each corner.
flag.symbolism: White stands for peace and purity, the taegeuk for the balance of opposing forces, and the four trigrams for heaven, earth, water and fire.

hook: South Korea is a white flag with a red-and-blue yin-yang circle and four black bar patterns in the corners; North Korea has stripes and a red star.
trivia: The flag is called the Taegukgi, and its trigrams come from the ancient Chinese divination text the I Ching.
A version of the flag was first used in 1883 by the Joseon dynasty.
